text:
Jon: Quick thread — proposal for a reserve on-demand floor + ephemeral spot burst pools to save cost while protecting hot routes. TL;DR: keep ~20% on-demand floor per region, allow spot bursting up to 3x baseline, and add graceful interruption handling and cross-region fallbacks.
Sara: Sounds good. How do we avoid dropped live requests when spots get preempted?
Jon: We route latency-sensitive traffic to on-demand by policy. Spot serves best-effort or background inference. On preempt, node daemon quickly marks pods and we retry on on-demand. Circuit-breaker: after 2 preempts within 10m for a given route, put new requests to on-demand.
Matt: Mechanism note: AWS/GCN provide 2-min interrupt signal / metadata. We'll run a small daemon that listens for it and triggers drain. Example drain command: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — but we should prefer graceful eviction where possible.
Lina: Also suggest a tiny warm on-demand pool per AZ (1-2 nodes) for hot models to avoid cold starts when we reroute. We'll need KV cache warming to reduce output degradation.
Emily: Doing some quick numbers — with 20% floor + 3x burst we estimate ~35-40% cost reduction on inference spend for non-enterprise tiers. Will validate with historical utilization. We need an SLO: p95 latency impact <= 5% when spot interruptions happen.
ops-bot: autoscaler: spot-pool policy triggered: scaled 8 -> 24 based on metric 'inflight_tokens' :rocket:
Matt: Edge cases: some regions have nearly zero spot capacity. Plan B is cross-region bursting (accept higher latency) or falling back to smaller quantized models. Need region-specific configs.
Jon: Sketch of config we can iterate on:
```yaml
nodePools:
  - name: spot-burst
    labels:
      capacity: spot
    taints:
      - key: spot, value: true, effect: NoSchedule
    autoscaling:
      minSize: 0
      maxSize: 48
      burstFactor: 3
reservePolicy:
  onDemandFloorPct: 20
  perRegion: true
circuitBreaker:
  preemptThreshold: 2
  windowSeconds: 600
```
Sara: Rollout plan? I suggest starting in staging (eu-west1) with one non-critical service, measure preempt rate, tail latency, and cost delta. :thumbsup:
Emily: I'll own telemetry. Need per-route metrics: token_cost, preempt_count, recovery_time, on_demand_fallback_count. Create alert: preempt_rate > 5% over 1h.
Lina: Also add a graceful downgrade flow: if on-demand capacity exhausted, fallback to smaller model or cached response set to keep p99 availability.
Jon: Action items: 1) Emily — telemetry & alerts, 2) Matt — interruption hooks + drain script + region overrides, 3) Lina — warm pool + model fallback prototype, 4) Sara — staging experiment and rollout checklist. I'll draft RFC with config and runbook.
capacity-bot: capacity-checker: notice: us-central1 spot_avail = LOW, recommend regional burstFactor override -> 2 for us-central1.
Matt: Got it, I'll add region overrides and include capacity-checker outputs in RFC.
Jon: Great — aim to have RFC + staging run next week, then post results here. Thanks all. :v:
